title: extcap/etwdump: bug fixes + cleanup after closure on windows
description:
Since signals aren't supported on Windows, extcap processes are killed with `TerminateProcess` on windows. With etwdump, this is an issue because it means that the ETW trace session is never de-registered and keeps hogging windows resources in the background. On most other extcaps, this wasn't really an issue because although killing the process is dirty, it didn't leave hanging stuff behind.

This PR:
- adds a new `--extcap-cleanup-postkill` that is called only when the extcap process is forcefully terminated (on linux, if graceful shutdown succeeds, it won't be called).
- fixes the fact that etwdump didn't allow a log level of 0 (because checking strtoul != 0 doesn't work if the number is 0). I also commented out ETW providers that do not display anything.
- fixes a minor bug with extcap when saving sub-options settings without changing them
- adds an example on how to use the table extcap element, also add a .bat script to make the extcap example runnable on Windows (shebangs don't work on Windows)

From what I understand from the thread, there's currently no way of cleaning up on Windows. If a better way is implemented, it will be easy to replace what I've done with it.

In the meantime however, this fixes the issue (at least for etw, along with a bunch of small improvements from the previous PR).
